faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial roof replacement in Irvington, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. Under the 25% rule in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, a commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a construction permit once roof work exceeds 25% of the total roof area in 12 months, so a full replacement always needs one. Confirm filing details with the Irvington construction office.

faqs.q: Does a commercial roof replacement in Irvington need historic-district approval?

runs.v: It can. A property in a historic district can need extra review for exterior roofing work, so confirm current requirements with the Irvington construction office. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: What is the best replacement membrane for an Irvington commercial building?

runs.v: It depends on the building, drainage, and budget: TPO and EPDM suit most flat roofs, modified bitumen handles foot traffic, built-up roofing suits heavy industrial decks, and white PVC or TPO cuts heat gain on a Springfield Avenue storefront.

faqs.q: Can my Irvington commercial building stay in use during the roof replacement?

runs.v: Usually, yes. The crew works in managed sections that keep unfinished areas weathertight and entrances open.

faqs.q: How does an infrared moisture survey scope an Irvington roof replacement?

runs.v: It maps wet insulation before tear-off: each warm anomaly on the ASTM C1153 survey gets a core cut, and the core-cut data rates each area wet or dry, which decides between a recover and a tear-off to the deck.
